name: Anova Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building anova — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary anova tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building anova — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary anova tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting anova work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to anova (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. When anova decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. When multiple anova strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Keep anova outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
6. Prefer the simplest anova approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Validate anova outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
8. When anova guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
9. Prefer explicit, readable anova solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen anova approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
11. Check that anova terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
12. Keep anova changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated anova concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop anova edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic anova advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of anova correctness.
- Do not skip documenting anova assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these anova guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
